articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. A few weeks ago, during a trip to the Philippines, I made my way across congested Manila to Bantayog ng mga Bayani, the memorial in Quezon City to Filipinos who resisted Ferdinand Marcos. The Wall of Remembrance outside, inscribed with the names of those who died resisting, was overrun with grass. I asked one guard where to find the museum, then another, before finding it around a corner. The receptionist asked who I was with. I told her I was a professor and researcher. She indicated to me that there were no tours on Monday and that I’d be free to tour the museum on my own. We sent a clear message on Election Day about what we want from the next Congress—affordability, accountability, and an economy that works for all. We’re disgusted with empty promises from a government that lavishes ever more on the do-nothing rich while working families fall further into the margins. We’ve had it with CEOs pocketing obscene sums while doling out scraps to everyone else and with billionaires frittering away huge sums to divide us. But tens of millions of working people just took back the wheel. We demonstrated how powerful we are when we come together. We showed that the future belongs to us , not to the 1 percent. articles.title: Single-Payer Healthcare Deadlock
articles.author: Larry Gross
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. California would seem to be the most likely state to enact a true single-payer healthcare program [SP]. After all, SP is favored by majorities, including Republicans. However, successive legislative efforts to pass CalCare, the SP plan sponsored by the California Nurses Association [CNA], have been killed by Democratic leaders before they could come to a vote. Actually, that’s not quite true: SP bills were passed by the CA legislature twice, when Republican governor Arnold Schwarzenegger promised to veto them. articles.title: War Budget Is a Path to Spiritual Death
articles.author: Ryan Wentz
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. In the coming weeks, Congress will be voting on Trump’s proposed $1.5 trillion war budget, double the number it was under Biden, which, of course, was already far too high. If passed, the U.S. military budget will be larger than the military budgets of the next 34 countries combined. Thirty-four countries combined. What’s more, while the Pentagon has been audited eight times, not once has it passed. articles.title: Inside the Epic Battle Over Control of a CA Grocery Union
articles.author: Chris Brooks
articles.content_excerpt: Eric Marcuz is one of the most naturally gifted rank-and-file organizers I have ever met. Overflowing with passion for his union, love for his coworkers, and C4 Energy drinks, he has been spending what little time he has outside of working full time as a dairy clerk at a Safeway grocery store in Redding, California, driving for hours to visit grocery stores across the state and talk with his fellow union members. Marcuz is running for president of United Food and Commercial Workers (UFCW) Local 8–Golden State as part of the At What Cost slate, a group of seven rank-and-file grocery workers who are committed to giving their coworkers something that should be taken for granted: an opportunity to choose who leads their union. articles.title: Resistance Runs Deep
articles.author: Joe Simpson
articles.content_excerpt: Resistance Runs Deep Lessons of Collective Action and Solidarity from the Underground Railroad At The Water’s Edge In the 1800s, the deep, dark currents of the Detroit River held both danger and deliverance. On the last stretch of a grueling journey, freedom seekers might find themselves at the water’s edge, hearts pounding with fear and anticipation. On the opposite shore lay Canada, where slavery had been abolished and a new life finally hovered within reach. No more stolen labor, stooping over crops sunup to sundown for enslavers’ profit. No more whipping posts and auction blocks and families ripped apart. articles.title: Anwar Shaikh Gave Us an Emancipatory Economics
articles.author: Clara E. Mattei
articles.content_excerpt: Writing about someone who has changed your life and to whom you owe so much is much more difficult than I would have thought. It is impossible to feel capable of delivering even a fraction of what it would take to fully honor the human and intellectual memory of Anwar Shaikh. I met Anwar at a moment of great intellectual insecurity for myself that he helped me overcome. Now, in front of this blank page, that insecurity is back. At the same time, this state of mind allows me to fully reconnect with the memories of our first encounters and the development of a mentorship and friendship that has deeply shaped me as a scholar and as a person. articles.title: The Executioner and the Loyalist: How Harvard Spent Summer 2026 Gutting Its Largest Union for Financial Gain
articles.author: Working Mass: The Massachusetts DSA Labor Outlet
articles.content_excerpt: A sign held up at the joint HGSU-HAW strike picket line in November 2026, referencing sister union HUCTW’s culling months before (Working Mass) By: Tony A, Adrian Aliano CAMBRIDGE – With the first strike by their workers that year abated, and two other unions’ anger rising, Harvard executives spent the summer of 2026 carrying out far-reaching cuts that gutted the ranks of the largest union on campus: the Harvard Union of Clerical and Technical Workers (HUCTW). In the end, hundreds of people were kicked out of the halls of the university to which they dedicated their lives, just for Harvard leaders to report exorbitant earnings made off their backs only weeks later. articles.title: The Scandal of Flávio Bolsonaro’s Escape Won’t Fade Away
articles.author: Felipe Antunes de Oliveira
articles.content_excerpt: To exfiltrate means “to smuggle [an intelligence agent, soldier, etc.] out of an area under enemy control.” The term belongs to military jargon, rather than to political commentary. Nevertheless, the Brazilian media has been using it to describe the sudden removal of former presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro from Brazil’s territory a couple of days after he lost the second round of this year’s presidential elections. José Roberto de Toledo, a veteran journalist, was probably the first to use the word “exfiltration” in relation to Flávio Bolsonaro, in his influential weekly podcast . The circumstances of Bolsonaro’s escape seem to come directly out of a spy film. articles.title: The Dominican Government Uses Zionism to Whitewash Trujillo
articles.author: Simón Rodríguez
articles.content_excerpt: On August 24, the Dominican government announced its adherence to the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance’s (IHRA) definition of antisemitism. President Luis Abinader , a businessman of Lebanese descent, made the announcement at the opening ceremony of the Sixth Latin American Forum Against Antisemitism,held in Santo Domingo by the US-based Combat Antisemitism Movement (CAM). Abinader also promised to invest 50 million pesos (approximately US$852,000) in the construction of a Jewish museum in Sosúa, in the north of the country, where 747 European Jewish refugees settled during the 1940s. Before the recent midterm election, the thirty-six-year-old East Lansing, Michigan native was exactly the sort of candidate who, according to conventional wisdom, could maybe beat establishment Democrats in liberal blue districts but would lack traction against the Right in a general election.
